facts.subject: Hester
facts.fact: Hester has not slept a full night since the Heron.
facts.quote: She had not slept a night through since the Heron

facts.subject: chapter
facts.fact: The scene begins before dawn and progresses to grey morning light.

facts.subject: Hester
facts.fact: Hester knows three loose roof tiles have been reset with fresh pitch.
facts.quote: three of them, which had been loose since the summer and which she had meant to see to, had been reset and bedded in fresh pitch

facts.subject: Ansel
facts.fact: Ansel knows Hester's grandmother sleeps directly under the eave.
facts.quote: Your grandmother's window is directly below

facts.subject: Hester's house
facts.fact: A previously unseen ladder stands against the eave with a lantern hung from the ridge.
facts.quote: A ladder stood against the eave of her own house, a plain ladder she had never seen, with its feet packed in the snow, and at the top of it, on the roof, a lantern hung from the ridge on a hook

facts.subject: Ansel
facts.fact: Ansel is wearing every coat he owns and using a flat shovel to clear ice.
facts.quote: in every coat he owned, with a flat shovel in both hands

facts.subject: Ansel
facts.fact: Ansel's right wrist is bound with a strip of grey linen, self-applied.
facts.quote: The wrist was bound now, a strip of grey linen wound under the cuff by a man who had not been taught, with the ends tucked in anyhow

facts.subject: Ansel
facts.fact: Ansel has a steady fine tremor from the shoulders down that worsens when he stops working.
facts.quote: It was a steady fine tremor from the shoulders down, like a tension carried through every stitch of a fabric

facts.subject: Ansel
facts.fact: Ansel's right hand is his only functional hand on that side.
facts.quote: It is the only one I have on this side

facts.subject: Ansel
facts.fact: Ansel is suffering from 'the Grey', a deep cold that no stove or coat reaches, common in newcomers.
facts.quote: The Grey sat on him under all the coats. She knew it was there as she knew a dropped stitch in her own knitting

facts.subject: world
facts.fact: The town accepts unexplained good fortune without questioning its source.
facts.quote: a town will accept a great deal of its own luck without asking where it came from

facts.subject: Ansel
facts.fact: Ansel does repairs anonymously at night to avoid thanks or reciprocity.
facts.quote: He had put the work where it could not be thanked. It was a seam worked on the wrong side of the cloth, where no thumb would ever run along it

planted.detail: Hester holds a blue ball and needles in the workroom.
planted.quote: the blue ball in her lap and the needles laid across her knee

planted.detail: The Kettle Room's shutter used to bang in every wind.
planted.quote: The shutter of the Kettle Room, which had banged in every wind since the autumn, had gone quiet
Chalk showed at both cuffs even from the lane

planted.detail: Ansel previously fell repeatedly on the shingle while the school watched.
planted.quote: watched him go down and get up and go down, with the whole school shrieking

planted.detail: The lane gate now closes with a click instead of a shriek.
planted.quote: the gate that no longer shrieked closed behind him with a click
